history.summary: NON-HINDU: THIS IS A JAIN (DIGAMBARA) TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: several Digambar Jain temples exist in Meerut; this entry documents the one travel portals (Tour My India, Yometro) list under the generic name 'Digambar Jain Temple Meerut', located at Irrigation Colony, Pallavpuram. It is dedicated to Parshvanath (emerald presiding image) and houses a 6-ft Padmasana Mahavir; the courtyard has 7 altars with 7 spires, the first called 'Tihkal Wale Baba', said to fulfil devotees' wishes; Yometro adds a 7-ft Parshvanath with 11 serpent hoods and 720 idols, and dates it ~100 years. If the CSV intended another listing it needs correction: the historic Shri Shantinath Digambar Jain Temple at Teergaran (built 1801 by Raja Harsukh Rai, said to be Meerut's oldest Jain temple), the Shantinath temple at Topkhana (c.130 years, built by the Chiranji Lal Jain family), the white-marble Shantinath temple at Saket, or the Mahavir temple at Jain Nagar are all separate shrines. CONFLICTING HOURS: Tour My India says morning-to-evening daily; Yometro says 'open 24 hours' and separately 5:00-11:30 AM / 5:30-8:30 PM - verify. BEST TIME CONFLICT: Tour My India says Oct-Feb; Yometro says May-Aug - verify.
